A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CREAM research work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original CREAM and baseline experiments on Llama-2 and Llama-3 in Section 4, with additional experiments and analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments, including downstream benchmark scores, arena comparisons, reward-ranking evaluations, and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same intrinsic rewarding, cross-iteration ranking consistency, and consistency-weighted DPO/reversed-DPO training procedure. The appendix variants are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Open Assistant training data, ARC-Easy/Challenge, OpenBookQA, SIQA, GSM8K, RewardBench, curated preference data, and arena evaluation. No task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The actual comparator sets remain unchanged, including SRLM, Oracle, SRLM + KL, ensemble methods, and Distilled DPO. Removing GPT-4o from the arena discussion does not remove an evaluated comparator: Figure 3 identifies it as the judge in both versions.

E3.justification: The data construction, model configurations, training budgets, decoding procedures, and evaluation metrics are unchanged. The appendix experiments retain their original settings, including extended iterations and larger or initially unaligned models.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix C retain the same analyses of rewarding, consistency measurements, extended training, weighted DPO, ensembles, data-specific consistency, model applicability, and prompt rewarding.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same plus/minus reporting, and statistical reporting elsewhere is unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 removes the reported qualitative finding that CREAM's win and tie rates improve against GPT-4o, retaining that finding only for Oracle. All numerical table and figure results remain unchanged; for example, Table 1 retains the Llama-3 CREAM M3 average of 83.37.

T1.justification: The definitions, objectives, theorems, lemmas, and Appendix B proofs are unchanged, as are the mathematical analyses in Appendix C. Correcting iteration arrows in Appendix C.6 is typographical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a generalized iterative preference-tuning framework and consistency regularization to mitigate rewarding bias and improve alignment.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, applicability qualifications, and Appendix A limitations are retained. The arena correction changes the attributed empirical comparison, while leaving its interpretation as evidence of improvement across iterations unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation details, hyperparameters, data preparation descriptions, and code-access link are unchanged. Appendix text flowing onto different pages adds no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including Section 2 and Appendix C.4's discussion of ensemble methods and robust preference optimization.

P1.justification: v5 makes a localized wording correction to the arena paragraph, replaces malformed iteration arrows in Appendix C.6, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The section organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v5 standardizes CREAM typography in several passages, captions, and table labels, with small spacing adjustments and appendix text reflow. All five figures and thirteen tables are retained without substantive display restructuring.

improvement.justification: v5 corrects Section 4.2's unsupported statement about improvement against GPT-4o: Figure 3 consistently identifies GPT-4o as the judge, while Oracle is an opponent. This improves agreement between the narrative and evidence. Minor typographical fixes also help readability; the methods, experiments, numerical results, and proofs otherwise remain unchanged.
